consigna.es: Escucha el mensaje. ¿Qué piensa el hablante de la noticia?

items.audio: Guess what, the woman next door, she's only gone and landed a promotion! Honestly, I'd never have guessed, because she always seemed so noncommittal in meetings. Mind you, she does bend over backwards for everyone, so fair enough. Anyway, I think we should get her a card.
opciones: It is a surprise, but she deserves it.
She should not have got it, as she hardly speaks in meetings.
It is hard to believe, so somebody should check first.

feedback.es: La noticia le sorprende, pero con «mind you… fair enough» admite que ella hace más que los demás y lo merece.

consigna.es: Escucha. ¿Qué quería decir la hermana con su comentario?

items.audio: When I told my sister I had been picked to organise the whole party, she said, “Oh, what a relaxing weekend that will be.” I have had the guest list, the budget and the food to sort out since March. Then she laughed, and offered to bring the cake. Fair point, I suppose.
opciones: That the weekend will be a good rest for the speaker.
That organising the party will be hard work.
That the speaker should refuse to organise it.

feedback.es: Decir «qué fin de semana tan relajante» cuando hay lista de invitados, presupuesto y comida por resolver es sarcasmo: quiere decir que será agotador.

consigna.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz. ¿Cuál es la postura de Mia sobre el piso?

items.audio: Hi, it's Mia. Thanks for showing us the flat yesterday. It is lovely, honestly, and I suppose it could work for us. It is a bit pricey, though, so we would rather not commit at this stage. Could you hold it for us until we have checked the budget? I will get back to you by Friday.
opciones: She has turned it down and is being polite about it.
She likes it so much that she will take it.
She is interested but is not ready to decide yet.

feedback.es: Dice que es precioso y que podría servirles, pero el precio le frena y pide que se lo reserven hasta decidir: está interesada, sin decidir aún.

consigna.es: Escucha. ¿Qué está haciendo el hablante en este momento?

items.audio: Thank you, all three of you. Let me recap, because I think we agree more than it seems. Two of you find the plan tempting, but nobody is sure the budget will hold. Having said that, I am hearing that you would back it if there were a safeguard. Moving on, then: should the fee rise if demand falls? Who would like to start?
opciones: Criticising the plan because it lacks a budget
Summarising what was said and moving the panel on
Closing the debate because nobody can agree

feedback.es: Recapitula lo dicho («let me recap», «I am hearing that») y cierra con «moving on»: resume las posturas y reconduce el debate.

consigna.es: Lee el correo. ¿Por qué dejó el tema la madre anfitriona?

items.texto: Hi Jo, a small misunderstanding at dinner last night. My host mother asked whether I wanted to join her at the market on Saturday, and I said, “We will see,” because I was keen but unsure about my plans. She smiled, said, “Of course,” and quickly changed the subject, so I thought nothing more of it at the time. Afterwards my host brother explained that in their family “We will see” is a gentle way of saying no. Honestly, I felt embarrassed, because I do want to go. I am going to text her this morning, and I can hardly blame her for not asking twice. Mia
opciones: She took Mia's answer as a polite refusal.
She was offended by something Mia said at dinner.
She had already found somebody else to go with.
She forgot that she had invited Mia.

feedback.es: El hermano explica que «We will see» es una forma suave de decir no; por eso ella entendió un rechazo cortés y no insistió.

consigna.es: Lee el comunicado. ¿Cuál es la postura real de la asociación?

items.texto: Dear resident, the association has taken note of your complaint about the shared garden and regrets any inconvenience. We had a frank exchange of views at Tuesday's meeting, and we remain committed to keeping the space clean for everyone. At this stage, however, we are not in a position to promise a date for the work, and we would ask you to bear in mind that the budget has been tight all year. We will get back to you once the committee has reconsidered the matter, and we hope that the garden can then be enjoyed by all residents again. Yours sincerely, the Residents' Association
opciones: It has agreed to clean the garden by next week.
It understands the complaint but offers no guarantee.
It believes the complaint was unfair to the committee.

feedback.es: «Take note», «frank exchange of views», «not in a position to promise» y «reconsidered» son fórmulas corteses: reconocen la queja sin garantizar nada.

consigna.es: Lee el relato. ¿Qué debe sospechar el lector?

items.texto: I want to be clear about last Friday. I stayed in all evening, reading by the window, and I heard nothing unusual, not even the dog next door. My brother says he saw me near the harbour at ten, but he has always exaggerated, and he has never let me forget the business with the boat. The police officer asked about my boots, which were by the door, still wet. I told him it had rained earlier, which was true, although I did not mention that it had stopped by six. Naturally, I was home all night. Ask anyone you like, and you will find that my version of events has never changed.
opciones: That the brother is inventing a story to cause trouble
That the police officer has confused the narrator with someone else
That the narrator was out that night and is hiding it

feedback.es: Las botas mojadas y que la lluvia había parado a las seis contradicen su versión: es un narrador poco fiable que oculta haber salido.

consigna.es: Lee el resumen. ¿Cómo valoran los autores su propio resultado?

items.texto: A new survey of 300 teenagers suggests that those who sleep longer tend to score higher in exams. The authors, however, stop short of claiming a causal link. Only one school took part, and the sleep hours were self-reported, so some pupils may have exaggerated. The pupils were also all the same age, which limits how far the findings apply to other teenagers. Nor can the team rule out that confident, well-organised pupils simply sleep better and also study better. In their view, the finding is worth following up carefully with a larger and more varied sample, but it is too early to advise parents using these figures alone.
opciones: As strong evidence that sleeping longer improves marks
As an encouraging result that still cannot show a cause
As proof that confident pupils, not sleep, explain the marks
As too weak to be worth following up

feedback.es: Dicen que solo sugiere una relación, no descartan otras explicaciones y piden una muestra mayor: es alentador, pero no prueba una causa.

consigna.es: Completa con el eco que muestra sorpresa.

items.texto: “Honestly, I'd turn down an offer that meant moving abroad.” “___? I'd accept it straight away.”

feedback.es: «I'd turn down» es «I would turn down» (tras «had» iría un participio). El eco repite el auxiliar y mantiene la polaridad: «Would you?».

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que completa la concesiva.

items.texto: Strict ___ the new rules may seem, nobody can claim they were applied unfairly.

feedback.es: «Strict though the rules may seem» es la estructura adjetivo + though + sujeto + may. «However» va delante del adjetivo; despite y unless no encajan.

items.texto: ___ demand fall, we will draw on the cash reserve to pay the rent.

feedback.es: «Should + sujeto + infinitivo» sustituye a «if» en condicionales formales de posibilidad remota: «Should demand fall…».

consigna.es: Completa con la inversión que exige «Not until».

items.texto: Not until the final slide ___ how much the speaker had left out.

feedback.es: Tras «Not until…» al inicio se invierte auxiliar y sujeto: «did the audience realise». Las demás mantienen el orden normal.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que completa la expresión.

items.texto: I was about to pay when it ___ on me that my wallet was gone, and my face went hot.

feedback.es: «It dawned on me that…» significa «caí en la cuenta de que…»: la expresión fija usa dawn.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que completa la frase.

items.texto: Saying that “all teenagers are lazy” is a sweeping ___: one exception is enough to make it fall apart.

feedback.es: Una «sweeping generalisation» es una afirmación demasiado amplia que una sola excepción desmiente.

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que completa la colocación.

items.texto: A flawed design can ___ doubt on every result that follows from it.

feedback.es: La colocación es «cast doubt on»: poner en duda. «Lend weight to» haría lo contrario, reforzaría.

consigna.es: Completa con la palabra que describe un vínculo engañoso.

items.texto: Ice cream sales and swimming accidents both rise in July, but the link is ___: hot weather drives both.

feedback.es: Si el calor explica ambas subidas, el vínculo no es causal: es «spurious», una correlación engañosa.

consigna.es: Rebate con tacto el cobro de entrada al parque (3-4 frases).

items.texto: Tu vecino propone cobrar entrada al parque del barrio. Reconoce su ambición, rebátelo con firmeza y sugiere otra opción.
items.respuesta: Much as I admire the ambition of the plan, I have reservations about the fee. It is by no means the fairest option for families with three children. What matters is that the park stays open to everyone. I would suggest a small donation instead.
aceptadas: However much I admire the idea, I am not convinced by the fee. Charging families would be far from fair. What matters is that the park remains free for everyone. I would suggest a small donation instead.

Much as I appreciate the effort, I cannot back the fee, which is by no means fair to large families. What matters is the cost, and it is families who would pay. I would propose a small donation instead.

feedback.es: Concede algo con «Much as I admire…», expresa reservas («I have reservations», «by no means»), menciona la tarifa y propone una alternativa.

consigna.es: Resume el estudio y sus límites para tu grupo (3-4 frases).

items.texto: Datos: 300 alumnos; quienes duermen más sacan mejores notas; participó un solo colegio; las horas de sueño las contaron ellos mismos.
items.respuesta: The study suggests that teenagers who sleep longer score higher in exams. However, the authors stop short of claiming a causal link. Only one school took part, and the sleep hours were self-reported, so the figures may be biased.
aceptadas: The survey suggests that pupils who sleep more get better marks, but the authors cannot rule out other factors. A single school took part, and the hours were self-reported, so the results may be biased. A causal link is not justified yet.

feedback.es: Usa un verbo cauteloso («suggests»), evita afirmar causa («stop short of a causal link») y cita una limitación concreta (un solo colegio, datos autoinformados).

notes: Revisados los 18 ítems: clave única, distractores plausibles, vocabulario dentro de N1-N10 y longitudes dentro de tabla.
P1 escucha.3: el audio permitía defender 'lo rechazó con cortesía'; ahora pide reservar el piso hasta decidir y la consigna pregunta por la postura de Mia.
P1 gramatica.1: 'Didn't you?' vs 'Did you?' era discutible; sustituido por eco de 'I'd turn down' (Would you?), con distractores Had/Did/Do inequívocamente incorrectos.
P1 lectura.4: distractores absolutos (conclusive/ignored completely) delataban la clave; reescritos como lecturas moderadas y plausibles (incluye la explicación alternativa de los alumnos confiados).
P1 lectura.2: la clave repetía 'promise' del pasaje; parafraseada (understands the complaint but offers no guarantee).
P2 lectura.1: modismo 'benefit of the doubt' mal usado; corregido y pasaje ampliado para cumplir las 105 palabras mínimas.
P2 gramatica.2: distractor 'because' sustituido por 'however' (trampa real); escritura.1/2: grupos de evidencias ampliados con variantes naturales.
Discriminación: el nivel se cubre de principio (bloque 1) a final (research discussion/critical analysis); escucha.2 y lectura.1 son los más accesibles y se dejan como ítems de entrada del nivel.
